alternate_names: Sri Valli Deva Sena Sameda Sri Karthikeya Swamy Temple
deities: Kartikeya (Murugan) flanked by Valli and Devasena (presiding deity)
Narthana Ganapati, Dakshina Murti, Vishnu, Brahma, Durga and Chandikeswarar (praharam shrines)

history.dynasty: None (modern; built by the Tamil community of Chandigarh)
history.period: Late 1980s-1992; Mahakumbhabhishekam January 1992; second Kumbhabhishekam 29 April 2002
history.summary: A Tamil Murugan temple in Sector 31-D, Chandigarh, founded by the city's Tamil community at the peak of Punjab's 1980s militancy: devotees first worshipped a vel (spear) on a pedestal in secret, chanting Tiruppugazh, and decided to build a full temple once the region was free of militancy around 1990. Sthapati Rajagopal and his disciple Sthapati Thiagarajan of Chennai designed it in Dravidian style with a mixed Chola-Pallava gopuram; idols were sculpted at Mahabalipuram. The deity was named 'Lord Karttikeya Swami' by the Maha Swami of the Kanchi Sankara Mutt; Kanchipuram Shivacharyas performed the Mahakumbhabhishekam in January 1992 and again on 29 April 2002 (Hanuman and Navagraha sannidhis were added after 2002). It is managed by the Lord Murugan Bhaktha Samaj at the Air Force Temple Complex, Sector 31-D.

name: Sri Karthikeya Swamy Temple
state: Chandigarh (Union Territory; CSV state 'Haryana' is incorrect)
town_description: Chandigarh is the planned city designed by Le Corbusier and serves as the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana while being a Union Territory itself. Its sectors are numbered in a grid; Sector 31 is in the city's southern zone, near the industrial area and the Air Force station. The temple sits inside the Air Force Temple Complex on Sector 31-D.

travel.railway: Chandigarh Railway Station - about 6-8 km (verify); autos and taxis available.
travel.road: Air Force Temple Complex, Sector 31-D, Chandigarh 160047; ISBT Sector 17 is about 6 km away (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Skanda Sashti and Thai Poosam are the major festival days (verify dates).
